channel.title: Acme: Light News
channel.description: Positive, lighthearted and unusual current news.

item.title: Twin brothers make MLB umpiring history together
item.description: Austin and Tyler Jones worked the same major league games for the first time during an Orioles-Blue Jays doubleheader in Baltimore. The twin brothers grew up playing together in South Carolina, turned to umpiring after college and reached the majors along separate paths before a rainout reshuffled the crews and reunited them on the field.

item.title: Skid Row talent show puts residents center stage
item.description: A dozen homeless or formerly homeless performers sang and danced at what organizers believe was Los Angeles' Skid Row's first talent show. The outdoor event gave participants a stage for original songs, movement and personal stories while neighbors gathered to cheer them on in a community better known for hardship.

item.title: Truck driver's handmade New York becomes museum exhibit
item.description: Truck driver Joe Macken spent two decades building a sprawling model of New York City from balsa wood and foam board, eventually creating more than 800,000 structures. The intricate cityscape—including both the Twin Towers and One World Trade Center—is now on display at the Museum of the City of New York.

item.title: An amateur archaeologist uncovers Germany's biggest Hadrian-era coin hoard
item.description: Oliver Riedl knew he had found more than a few Roman coins when his metal detector kept beeping in a field near Cologne. Experts ultimately recovered 934 silver denarii weighing 6.8 pounds, Germany's largest hoard from Emperor Hadrian's era. The cache, likely buried for safekeeping in the second century, is now on museum display.

item.title: Those extra reusable bags can get a useful second life
item.description: The reusable bags multiplying under the sink do not need to become trash. Food pantries, shelters and reuse shops may welcome clean extras, while keeping a small set visible in the car or by the door makes actual reuse more likely. Experts say repeated use—not merely owning the bags—is what delivers the environmental benefit.

item.title: Fat Bear Week opens with 1,200-pound champion Chunk defending his crown
item.description: Online voting has begun in the 12th Fat Bear Week, where 16 brown bears from Alaska's Katmai National Park compete in a single-elimination bracket. Reigning champion Chunk, estimated at 1,200 pounds last year, faces challengers including Gully, the offspring of two-time winner Grazer. The winner will be announced Sept. 29.

item.title: Singing lemurs borrow a soprano's trick to carry a tune
item.description: Indris in Madagascar widen their mouths as their notes rise, tuning their vocal tract much as opera singers do so songs travel through dense rainforest. Researchers studying 83 recordings say the duets mark territory and help the critically endangered lemurs keep social bonds.

item.title: Mississippi's raccoon boot camp teaches orphaned kits to go wild
item.description: At Woodside Wildlife Rescue, orphaned raccoons spend about six months learning to forage, fish, dodge predators and distrust human traps. After their woodland lessons, each class graduates with music and a blessing before the young raccoons are released into the Mississippi forest.

item.title: A five-panel artwork will soar over a dinosaur in Toronto
item.description: The Royal Ontario Museum is installing Raphaël Barontini's largest work above its Futalognkosaurus. Five immense dyed and screen-printed panels weave migration, resistance and cultural exchange from images in the museum's collections. The main-floor installation opens Saturday and will be free this fall.

item.title: Salzburg opens a museum where von Trapp history meets Hollywood
item.description: A new Sound of Music museum at Salzburg's Hellbrunn Palace pairs the real von Trapp family's story with the movie that made it famous. Its 450 objects include costumes, props and recordings, while the nearby gazebo gives visitors a familiar place to sing along.

item.title: The equinox arrives Wednesday, but equal day and night come later
item.description: The September equinox falls Wednesday at 1:05 a.m. British time, beginning astronomical autumn in the north and spring in the south. Day and night will not be precisely equal, because the sun is a disc and Earth's atmosphere bends its light; Britain's “equilux” follows Friday.

item.title: A sophisticated heist makes off with more than 800,000 bees
item.description: Thieves stole 44 bee colonies—more than 800,000 bees—from several properties in far north Queensland. Investigators say the careful removal of brood boxes points to experienced beekeepers, and suspect the colonies may be headed for avocado orchards as pollination season begins.

item.title: Captain America and R2-D2 light up the Lucas Museum opening
item.description: A drone show sent Captain America, R2-D2, the Millennium Falcon and Shrek's dragon across the sky above the new Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles. George Lucas and Mellody Hobson's spaceship-shaped museum celebrated with a gala before opening its visual-storytelling collection to the public Tuesday.

item.title: Officer climbs a lakeside tree to rescue a 23-year-old macaw
item.description: Blaze, a scarlet macaw startled by a dog, spent the night high above Michigan's Elberta Beach while his owner waited below. When a ladder truck could not reach him on the steep bluff, a Frankfort police officer used ropes to climb the tree and bring the 23-year-old bird safely back down.

item.title: Firefighters pull an unharmed kitten from a storm drain
item.description: Firefighters in Shelton, Connecticut, freed a kitten trapped in a storm drain Friday night. The little cat emerged unharmed, and town officials are now asking the public to help locate its family.
